verses.text: For the music director. To the tune "The Lilies." A thoughtful psalm of the sons of Korah. A wedding song. My heart is full of beautiful words as I recite my poem for the king. My tongue is like the pen of a skilled writer.
You are the most excellent of men. Your lips speak with grace, so God has blessed you forever.
Put your sword at your side, mighty warrior. Clothe yourself in splendour and majesty.
In your majesty ride out to victory for the sake of truth, humility, and what is right. Let your right hand do amazing things.
Your arrows are sharp. They pierce the hearts of the king's enemies. The nations fall at your feet.
Your throne, God, lasts forever and ever. You rule your kingdom with a fair sceptre.
You love what is right and hate what is evil. So God, your God, has chosen you above your companions by pouring on you the oil of joy.
All your robes smell of myrrh, aloes, and cassia. From palaces decorated with ivory, the music of stringed instruments makes you glad.
Daughters of kings are among the women you honour. At your right hand stands the queen, wearing gold from Ophir.
Listen, daughter. Think about this and pay attention. Forget your people and your father's family.
The king will be delighted by your beauty. Honour him, because he is your lord.
The people of Tyre will come with a gift. Rich people will try to win your favour.
The princess is in her rooms, looking glorious. Her gown is woven with gold.
She is led to the king in a beautifully embroidered dress. The young women, her friends who follow her, are brought to you.
They are led in with joy and gladness. They enter the king's palace.
Your sons will take the place of your ancestors. You will make them rulers over all the earth.
I will make your name remembered for all generations. So the nations will praise you forever and ever.
